summary:
**Visual resemblance: 8.2/10. Below the ≥9 acceptance threshold.** Substantial improvement over the rejected native UI: the player-first hierarchy, adjacent queue, charcoal cards, white transport, artwork, and selected-row treatment clearly resemble the web reference.

| Area | Score |
|---|---:|
| Hierarchy/layout | 8.5 |
| Proportions | 7.5 |
| Surfaces | 9 |
| Typography | 8.5 |
| Queue/thumbnails | 8.5 |
| Controls | 8 |
| Responsive usability | 7.5 |

Highest actionable issues:

- **Short-window media proportions diverge considerably.** At 760×680 the video is 688×226; at 1100×720 it is approximately 700×266. The web reference has a conventional 16:9 presentation. Adjust [NativeUIStyle.swift](/Users/gustavocaiano/.t3/worktrees/tubeshuffle/t3-310b873b/macos/TubeShuffle/App/NativeUIStyle.swift) `NativePlayerLayout` to balance viewport containment with aspect ratio, potentially reducing chrome or using a narrower centered media region. Actual media fitting/letterboxing remains unverified.
- **Queue and shuffle discoverability deteriorate at narrow sizes.** At 760×680 the queue starts exactly below the viewport, with shuffle settings farther down. Nothing visible signals their location. Add an obvious queue/settings navigation affordance or partial next-section reveal in [NativeLibraryView.swift](/Users/gustavocaiano/.t3/worktrees/tubeshuffle/t3-310b873b/macos/TubeShuffle/App/NativeLibraryView.swift:87).
- **Primary play silently implies shuffle.** Both ready-state play icons invoke `startQueue`, while the displayed artwork/title represents the first item. A user could reasonably expect that item to play. Make the visible action “Shuffle & listen,” or make the artwork play its displayed item. See `NativeIdleDeck` in [NativePlayerComponents.swift](/Users/gustavocaiano/.t3/worktrees/tubeshuffle/t3-310b873b/macos/TubeShuffle/App/NativePlayerComponents.swift).
- **Stop also closes the player, but its square icon does not communicate that consequence.** Provide a visible “Stop & close” label or distinct close action in `NativeTransport`. Tooltip/accessibility text helps, but does not establish immediate intuitiveness.

**Clipping:** No player/transport edge clipping is visible in the seven supplied captures. Measurements support containment for those cases. Queue scrolling, long-content extremes, recovery banners, and below-fold panels are not visually established by these captures.

**Evidence inspected:** root and playlist codemaps; the three requested native sources; relevant web layout/control source excerpts; both reference images; all seven actual SwiftUI captures; supplied measurements. No files changed or live media launched.

**Behavior/policy acceptance remains open.** The reported three passing tests were not rerun. Retained-player structure and explicit playback initiation are supported by source inspection, but synthetic paused events do not prove live playback, keyboard/media controls, persistence, account behavior, or library safety. Missing WKWebView compositor pixels are an evidence gap—not a demonstrated runtime failure. Full scrolled captures of shuffle settings and suggestions, plus compositor-inclusive media evidence, are needed before a ≥9 visual acceptance decision.
